title: The strong person controls themselves when angry
narrator: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
arabic: ليس الشديد بالصرعة إنما الشديد الذي يملك نفسه عند الغضب
english_translation: The strong person is not the one who defeats others in wrestling; the strong person is the one who controls himself when angry.
roman_urdu_translation: Taqatwar woh nahin jo kushti mein doosron ko pachhaad de, taqatwar woh hai jo gusse ke waqt apne aap par qaboo rakhe.
explanation: The Prophet ﷺ redefines strength as self-control in a moment of anger.

title: Do not become angry
narrator: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
explanation: The advice the Prophet ﷺ gave, and repeated, to a man who asked for counsel.
context: A man asked the Prophet ﷺ for advice. The Prophet ﷺ said 'Do not become angry', and the man asked again several times; each time the Prophet ﷺ repeated the same words.

title: The closest a servant is to their Lord is in prostration
narrator: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
arabic: أقرب ما يكون العبد من ربه وهو ساجد فأكثروا الدعاء
transliteration: Aqrabu ma yakunul-'abdu min rabbihi wa huwa sajid, fa akthirud-du'a'.
english_translation: The closest a servant is to his Lord is when he is prostrating, so make abundant supplication.
roman_urdu_translation: Banda apne Rab ke sab se zyada qareeb sajde ki halat mein hota hai, pas us mein bohat dua kiya karo.
explanation: An invitation to pour out one's requests in prostration.

title: Every disease has a cure
narrator: Jabir ibn 'Abdillah (may Allah be pleased with them both)
arabic: لكل داء دواء فإذا أصيب دواء الداء برأ بإذن الله عز وجل
transliteration: Likulli da'in dawa', fa idha usiba dawa'ud-da'i bara'a bi-idhnillahi 'azza wa jall.
english_translation: Every disease has a cure. When the cure is found for the disease, it is healed by the permission of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.
roman_urdu_translation: Har bimari ki dawa hai. Jab bimari ko uski dawa pahunch jaye to Allah ke hukm se shifa ho jati hai.
explanation: Seeking treatment is part of the Prophet's ﷺ teaching. This applies to physical illness and, in our time, to mental health care as well.

title: The affair of the believer is all good
narrator: Suhayb ibn Sinan (may Allah be pleased with him)
arabic: عجبا لأمر المؤمن إن أمره كله خير وليس ذاك لأحد إلا للمؤمن إن أصابته سراء شكر فكان خيرا له وإن أصابته ضراء صبر فكان خيرا له
transliteration: 'Ajaban li-amril-mu'min, inna amrahu kullahu khayr, wa laysa dhaka li-ahadin illa lil-mu'min. In asabat-hu sarra'u shakara fakana khayran lah, wa in asabat-hu darra'u sabara fakana khayran lah.
english_translation: How wonderful is the affair of the believer, for all of his affairs are good, and this is only for the believer. If something good happens to him, he is grateful, and that is good for him. If something harmful happens to him, he is patient, and that is good for him.
roman_urdu_translation: Momin ka muamla bhi ajeeb hai, uske liye har haal mein bhalai hai, aur yeh sirf momin ke liye hai. Agar usay khushi pahunche to shukr karta hai aur yeh uske liye behtar hai, aur agar takleef pahunche to sabr karta hai aur yeh bhi uske liye behtar hai.
explanation: Both gratitude in ease and patience in hardship are described as good for the believer.

title: No worry or grief touches a believer without it counting for them
narrator: Abu Sa'id al-Khudri and Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with them)
arabic: ما يصيب المسلم من نصب ولا وصب ولا هم ولا حزن ولا أذى ولا غم حتى الشوكة يشاكها إلا كفر الله بها من خطاياه
transliteration: Ma yusibul-muslima min nasabin wa la wasabin wa la hammin wa la huznin wa la adhan wa la ghammin hattash-shawkati yushakuha illa kaffarallahu biha min khataya'h.
english_translation: No fatigue, illness, worry, grief, harm or distress befalls a Muslim — even the prick of a thorn — except that Allah expiates some of his sins because of it.
roman_urdu_translation: Musalman ko jo bhi thakan, bimari, fikr, gham, takleef ya pareshani pahunchti hai, yahan tak ke kaanta bhi chubhta hai, Allah us ke badle us ke gunahon mein se kuch maaf kar deta hai.
explanation: The Prophet ﷺ names worry and grief explicitly. Your pain is seen, and it is not wasted. This does not say that you should not seek relief or help.

title: True patience is at the first shock
narrator: Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him)
english_translation: Patience is only at the first shock.
roman_urdu_translation: Sabr to pehle sadme ke waqt hi hai.
explanation: The Prophet ﷺ said this to a woman who was crying at a grave. It points to the first moment of loss as the place where patience matters most.
context: He passed a woman weeping at a grave and told her to fear Allah and be patient. She did not recognise him and answered sharply; when she learned who he was, she came to him and he said these words.

title: Do not say 'if only' — say 'Allah decreed, and what He willed, He did'
narrator: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
arabic: المؤمن القوي خير وأحب إلى الله من المؤمن الضعيف وفي كل خير احرص على ما ينفعك واستعن بالله ولا تعجز وإن أصابك شيء فلا تقل لو أني فعلت كان كذا وكذا ولكن قل قدر الله وما شاء فعل فإن لو تفتح عمل الشيطان
transliteration: Al-mu'minul-qawiyyu khayrun wa ahabbu ilallahi minal-mu'minid-da'if, wa fi kullin khayr. Ihris 'ala ma yanfa'uk, wasta'in billahi wa la ta'jiz. Wa in asabaka shay'un fala taqul: law anni fa'altu kana kadha wa kadha, wa lakin qul: qaddarallahu wa ma sha'a fa'al, fa inna law taftahu 'amalash-shaytan.
english_translation: The strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer, though there is good in both. Be keen on what benefits you, seek help from Allah, and do not give up. If something befalls you, do not say: 'If only I had done such-and-such, it would have been so-and-so.' Rather say: 'Allah has decreed, and what He willed, He did.' For 'if only' opens the door to the work of Satan.
roman_urdu_translation: Taqatwar momin Allah ke nazdeek kamzor momin se behtar aur zyada pasandeeda hai, aur dono mein bhalai hai. Us cheez ki koshish karo jo tumhein nafa de, Allah se madad mango aur himmat na haaro. Agar tumhein koi museebat pahunche to yeh na kaho ke agar main aisa kar leta to aisa ho jata, balke kaho: Allah ne muqaddar kiya aur jo us ne chaha kiya, kyunke 'agar' shaitan ke kaam ka darwaza kholta hai.
explanation: Advice for the mind that keeps replaying what could have been done differently: act on what you can, ask Allah for help, and leave what has passed with Allah's decree.

title: Your self has a right over you
narrator: Abu Juhayfah (may Allah be pleased with him)
arabic: إن لربك عليك حقا ولنفسك عليك حقا ولأهلك عليك حقا فأعط كل ذي حق حقه
transliteration: Inna lirabbika 'alayka haqqan, wa linafsika 'alayka haqqan, wa li-ahlika 'alayka haqqan, fa a'ti kulla dhi haqqin haqqah.
english_translation: Your Lord has a right over you, your self has a right over you, and your family has a right over you, so give each its due.
roman_urdu_translation: Tere Rab ka tujh par haq hai, tere nafs ka tujh par haq hai aur tere ghar walon ka tujh par haq hai, pas har haq wale ko uska haq ada kar.
explanation: Rest and care for oneself are named as a right alongside worship and family.
context: Salman al-Farisi (may Allah be pleased with him) said this to his brother Abu ad-Darda', who was fasting and praying through the nights and neglecting his family. When the Prophet ﷺ heard it, he said: 'Salman has spoken the truth.'

title: The religion is ease
narrator: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
arabic: إن الدين يسر ولن يشاد الدين أحد إلا غلبه فسددوا وقاربوا وأبشروا
transliteration: Innad-dina yusr, wa lan yushaddad-dina ahadun illa ghalabah. Fa saddidu wa qaribu wa abshiru.
english_translation: Indeed the religion is ease, and no one makes the religion difficult for themselves except that it overcomes them. So be moderate, strive to do what you can, and have good hope.
roman_urdu_translation: Beshak deen aasani hai, aur jo koi deen ko apne upar sakht kar le to woh us par ghalib aa jata hai. Pas meana ravi ikhtiyar karo, durustgi ki koshish karo aur khush khabri lo.
explanation: A reminder to approach worship and effort steadily and without exhausting oneself.

title: The eye weeps and the heart grieves
narrator: Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him)
arabic: إن العين تدمع والقلب يحزن ولا نقول إلا ما يرضى ربنا وإنا بفراقك يا إبراهيم لمحزونون
transliteration: Innal-'ayna tadma'u wal-qalba yahzanu wa la naqulu illa ma yarda rabbuna, wa inna bifiraqika ya Ibrahimu lamahzunun.
english_translation: The eye weeps and the heart grieves, and we say only what pleases our Lord. O Ibrahim, we are grieved at your departure.
roman_urdu_translation: Aankh aansu bahati hai aur dil ghamgeen hota hai, aur hum wohi kehte hain jis se hamara Rab razi ho. Ae Ibrahim! Hum tere bichhadne par ghamgeen hain.
explanation: The Prophet ﷺ's own words when his young son died. Grief and tears are natural and are not a failure of faith.
context: The Prophet ﷺ said this at the death of his son Ibrahim, while his eyes were shedding tears.

title: I am as My servant thinks of Me
narrator: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
arabic: أنا عند ظن عبدي بي وأنا معه إذا ذكرني
transliteration: Ana 'inda zanni 'abdi bi, wa ana ma'ahu idha dhakarani.
english_translation: I am as My servant thinks of Me, and I am with him when he remembers Me.
roman_urdu_translation: Main apne bande ke gumaan ke mutabiq hoon jo woh mere bare mein rakhta hai, aur main us ke saath hoon jab woh mujhe yaad karta hai.
explanation: A hadith qudsi: words that the Prophet ﷺ reported from Allah. It invites a hopeful view of Allah and describes His company with those who remember Him.

title: My mercy prevails over My wrath
narrator: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
english_translation: Indeed, My mercy has preceded My wrath.
roman_urdu_translation: Beshak meri rehmat mere ghazab par sabqat le gayi.
explanation: A hadith qudsi: Allah wrote this for Himself when He created the creation. Wordings differ slightly between narrations (e.g. 'prevails over' and 'precedes').
context: The Prophet ﷺ said: when Allah created the creation, He wrote in a Book that is with Him above the Throne: 'My mercy precedes My wrath.'

title: Entering the home: mention Allah
narrator: Jabir ibn 'Abdillah (may Allah be pleased with them both)
arabic: إذا دخل الرجل بيته فذكر الله عند دخوله وعند طعامه قال الشيطان لا مبيت لكم ولا عشاء
transliteration: Idha dakhalar-rajulu baytahu fadhakarallaha 'inda dukhulihi wa 'inda ta'amihi qalash-shaytanu la mabita lakum wa la 'asha'.
english_translation: When a man enters his house and mentions Allah upon entering and while eating, Satan says: 'You have no place to spend the night and no supper.'
roman_urdu_translation: Jab aadmi apne ghar mein dakhil hota hai aur dakhil hote waqt aur khana khate waqt Allah ka zikr karta hai to shaitan kehta hai: tumhare liye na yahan raat guzarne ki jagah hai na raat ka khana.
explanation: The Prophet ﷺ encouraged mentioning Allah's name on entering the home. A specific wording from other narrations is under review in this collection.
